f2_source_observed.observed_boundary: WP206 current-authority admission binds canonical path/device/inode plus authority-receipt identity; same-inode data/schema mutation is a separately preserved discriminator and is not closed by G4 repeat-provenance acceptance.

external_primary_sources.relevant_mechanism: PRAGMA data_version changes for commits by other connections, but not for commits performed by the same connection; values are local to a connection and intended for repeated comparison on that connection.

pager data-version changes on changes to the particular database file from either the same connection or other connections; SQLite documents this file-control as the mechanism covering both internal and external changes for one attached database.
schema_version is automatically incremented when the schema changes and therefore is not a general witness for ordinary row/data mutation.
SQLite transactions provide serializable isolation, but isolation orders/controls visibility; it does not authenticate that a pre-existing row is the exact historically evidenced row.

source_level_findings: PRAGMA data_version is insufficient as a complete WP206 authority fence because it deliberately omits changes made by the same database connection.
SQLITE_FCNTL_DATA_VERSION is a stronger low-level drift witness because SQLite states that it changes for both same-connection and other-connection changes to the particular database file.
schema_version is useful specifically for schema drift but cannot witness ordinary row/data mutation.
A SQLite change counter can be used as a cheap trigger for fail-closed revalidation, but it is not itself historical provenance or content authenticity and must not become a second truth authority.

Current WP206 source already guards pathname/device/inode replacement and validates the digest stored with the checkpoint row. E1 does not establish that this self-consistency check proves the row is the externally evidenced historical checkpoint; that question is reserved for architecture mapping/reproduction after duplicate-work reconciliation.

No source-level evidence justifies continuous whole-database hashing as the default hot-path mechanism; the current best-supported direction is a low-cost drift signal followed by bounded authoritative revalidation when triggered.
hypothesis: A low-overhead SQLite change witness can cheaply detect same-inode live drift and trigger bounded fail-closed revalidation without becoming canonical authority.
counterhypothesis: Available high-level SQLite counters are too connection-local/coarse to close WP206's authority gap, so explicit transaction-bound content/provenance revalidation may still be required.
decision: Do not promote PRAGMA data_version as a complete fix. Preserve it or a stronger equivalent only as a drift trigger; separately determine whether the exact historical checkpoint content is externally bound before designing a build candidate.
